clue.text: Nick, having returned, made a home in it

indicators.note: having returned says the word for making a home is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to make a home in a place is to have lived there

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick comes back to the house they once lived in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having returned' turns LIVED back to front, giving the letters of the answer. Old Nick is a traditional nickname for Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a long-standing English nickname for Satan, the evil one.

clue.text: Cook book to bring children up on

parts.note: to raise children is to bring them up

explanation.surface: A cookery book that is meant to help with bringing up the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is a way of cooking meat slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot.

clue.text: Jilted, moved from home

explanation.surface: Someone dumped by a partner and moving out of the shared home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one way it is an idiom for being abandoned by a lover; read literally it is leaving one's apartment, a flat being the British word for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jilted lover has been left high and dry, abandoned without warning; someone who moved out has quit their apartment.

clue.text: Pick a quarrel with the light heavyweight

parts.note: a star is a light in the sky
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: Picking a fight with the light-heavyweight boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light heavyweight' looks like a boxing division but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To start on someone is the idiom for beginning to attack or berate them.

clue.text: Does it have a souped up 60 engine?

definitions.text: Does it have a souped up 60 engine?

parts.words: Does it have a souped up 60 engine?
parts.note: souped up hints at stock, the base of soup, and the engine suggests a motor vehicle; such cars are modified for banger racing

explanation.surface: A question about a tuned-up old motor.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on 'souped up': stock is the base of soup, so a souped-up car becomes a stock one. The '60' may be an OCR misreading of the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing saloon car, often modified or souped up, used in a type of oval-track racing.

clue.text: Says the horse will carry the pack

indicators.note: will carry says the horse holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a hack is a horse, especially one hired for riding
avers means states or says firmly

explanation.surface: Someone declares the horse will bear the load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Says' looks like the verb introducing speech, but it supplies the filling; a hack is an ordinary riding horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack-style bag carried on the back is a pack for walkers.

clue.text: Girl that Irene was mistaken for

indicators.note: was mistaken says the letters of the two words are confused into another order

explanation.surface: A girl wrongly taken for someone named Irene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was mistaken' rearranges the nine letters of THAT IRENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Proceed quietly to help yourself to

explanation.surface: A thief creeping in and taking things.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is to move stealthily, the other to take without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To move silently is to creep; to take what is not yours is theft.

clue.text: Up to the L in Lincoln'

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the president's first name

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln
the letter L itself

explanation.surface: A quotation-style fragment about a letter in a name.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside ABE, the short form of Abraham Lincoln's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up to a task is to be capable of doing it.

clue.text: The clergyman needs a little rest, anyhow

parts.note: mini means little or small

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters of the following word are jumbled

explanation.surface: The vicar needs a short break, in any case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link word; 'little rest' tempts as a nap, but 'a little' is the size word and 'rest' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant clergyman, especially in nonconformist churches, is called this title.

clue.text: Does he retreat when it comes to putting up the money?

definitions.text: Does he retreat when it comes to putting up the money?

parts.words: Does he retreat when it comes to putting up the money?
parts.note: the question pretends the person is one who backs off, while in fact he supports a venture with funds

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man retreats when asked to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing away suggests retreat, but backing a venture means financing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial supporter of a project or show is its sponsor or investor.

clue.text: Water thoroughly

explanation.surface: Watering something thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a source of water dug in the ground, the other an adverb meaning fully.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft sunk for groundwater supplies water; done properly means done thoroughly.

clue.text: On the subject of actors, is dull

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over something
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A remark that, regarding actors, the whole troupe is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dull' describes weather here, not personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey, cloudy sky is described as dull weather.

clue.text: Feeling the chaps should have sent it round

indicators.note: round says the first pair of words goes around the chaps

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: A view that the men ought to have passed it around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent it' is taken as written and wraps the chaps, splitting after its fifth letter; 'should have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion or opinion felt about something is a feeling.

clue.text: Lets the waves engulf it

indicators.note: engulf says the waves swallow up the following word inside them

parts.note: perms are artificial waves put into hair

explanation.surface: Allowing the sea waves to swamp something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' looks like the sea, but it means hairdressing perms.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow something is to let it happen.

clue.text: Besides being further across

parts.note: more means further or additional
over can mean across, as in going over the road

explanation.surface: Something that goes beyond being even further across.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb adding a further point, synonym of in addition.

clue.text: Did one of his parents take him in?

definitions.text: Did one of his parents take him in?

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
to take someone in is to trick them

explanation.surface: A question about whether a boy was deceived by his mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a boy's name by describing his father fooling him.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so a boy who could have a father who fooled him.

clue.text: Lent approached ever nearer

explanation.surface: Someone lent money and kept coming closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the Christian season, but here it is a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Money advanced is lent ahead of time; an army that advanced moved forward.

clue.text: Where nurses work to get ahead

explanation.surface: A comment that hospital work is the way to get on in life.
explanation.walkthrough: Split two ways it says nurses are on the hospital wards; as one word it means forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurses are on hospital wards; going forward means going ahead.

clue.text: It's a fish egg, by the way

indicators.note: by means beside, so the street abbreviation sits next to the urging

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to egg someone is to urge them on

explanation.surface: A remark about fish roe, made in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish egg' suggests caviar, yet 'egg' is a verb meaning urge on, and 'by the way' gives ST beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large primitive fish famous as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Regards as verbal agreements

indicators.note: verbal says the word for agreement is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: ayes are votes of agreement

explanation.surface: Considering things as spoken agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: AYES, votes in favour, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something is to eye or regard it.

clue.text: Having competed against, we went inside and watched TV

indicators.note: went inside says the pair of letters is gone from the middle of the word

parts.note: to have watched television is to have viewed it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Having been rivals, the pair went indoors to watch television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' is a link word, as in competing against; the surface's 'we went inside' is the instruction to take the pronoun out of the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To have contended or striven with rivals is to have competed.

clue.text: A has-been star performing with nobodies in the film world

parts.note: ex means a former one, a has-been

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A faded celebrity now acting alongside unknown bit-part players.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' is a link word; 'has-been' supplies the prefix meaning former.
explanation.definitionFit: Film walk-ons with no lines are anonymous crowd players.

clue.text: Put up with the staff

explanation.surface: Tolerating the staff of employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but means a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to bear something; a walking pole is a staff.

clue.text: With the river in semi-flood, lay it on

indicators.note: in puts the river inside the jumbled letters
flood suggests letters washed into disorder

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: With the river partly flooding, someone lays it on thick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-flood' looks like a partial flood, but 'semi' is the fodder and 'flood' its anagram signal, giving IMSE around the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay a burden or tax on someone is to inflict or levy it.

clue.text: Make notes, but not in a neat form

indicators.note: form means shape, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Writing comments in an untidy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges NOT and A NEAT, with 'but' and 'in' as link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To add explanatory comments to a text is to gloss it.

clue.text: Stopped, indeed, when I had gone out

indicators.note: had gone says one letter leaves, and out says the rest are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something was over, indeed, once I had left.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I from INDEED and rearrange the remaining NDEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that finished has stopped or concluded.

clue.text: The dream of giving up work?

definitions.text: The dream of giving up work?

parts.words: The dream of giving up work?
parts.note: a fantasy of doing nothing at all, and a passing whim

explanation.surface: Daydreaming of retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical notion is literally the fancy of being without work.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream or passing whim is a vain fancy.
